findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin paths
findings.body: When `returnUrl` is attacker-controlled, passing it directly to `location.assign` enables external phishing redirects and potentially dangerous URL schemes such as `javascript:`. Validate it as an approved same-origin path before navigating.

findings.title: [P1] Redact issued tokens before auditing
findings.body: Every issued token is forwarded unchanged to `console.log`. In deployments that collect console output, anyone with log access can recover and replay still-valid bearer credentials. Audit only non-sensitive metadata or a non-reversible identifier.

findings.title: [P3] Fall back when trimming produces an empty name
findings.body: A cached whitespace-only name now becomes `""`, bypassing the `"Anonymous"` fallback and producing a blank display name. Apply the fallback after trimming if empty names are not valid.

findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin URLs
findings.body:
Passing an attacker-controlled return URL such as `javascript:...` can execute script in the authenticated origin; an absolute external URL also creates an open redirect suitable for phishing.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Redact issued tokens before auditing
findings.body:
Every call records the raw authentication token through `console.log`, exposing reusable credentials to browser/server logs and anyone with log access.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restrict `returnUrl` to approved same-origin paths
findings.body:
When `returnUrl` is attacker-influenced, values such as `https://evil.example` create an open redirect, while `javascript:...` URLs can execute script in the application origin unless separately blocked. This affects login flows that obtain the return URL from query parameters or client-controlled state.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued authentication tokens to audit logs
findings.body:
Every valid token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is forwarded to `console.log`, exposing bearer credentials to browser consoles or centralized log collectors. Anyone with log access can replay a still-valid token and impersonate its holder.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
